Generative AI Framework for Telecom 
Project Risk Management 
 
 
Abstract— 
Today's telecom deployment projects are extremely 
complex, with strict regulatory service -level 
agreements, cost -effective infrastructure investments, 
and ever -changing risks. Manual risk management 
practices are limited by subjectivity and face significant 
challenges in terms of fragmented risk registers, slow 
risk mitigation response times and inconsistent risk 
assessment. The proposed hybrid product -and-
research application is based on the use of Generative 
Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) tools to automa te risk 
identification, impact assessment, and real -time 
mitigation recommendations. The tool was built in 
Python, with the help of a special domain risk 
knowledge base and Large Language Model (LLM) 
APIs, and it becomes an active assistant for project 
management divisions. To assess its effectiveness, a 
mixed methods research approach will be used that 
looks at comparing AI -generated risk assessments 
against the baseline human-expert risk assessment. The 
quantitative evaluation will be based on alignment 
scoring, semantic similarity and processing latency, and 
the qualitative evaluation will be based on blind expert 
reviews conducted using a Likert scale based on both 
the utility and the accuracy of the results and the ability 
to act based on those results. 
Keywords 
Generative AI, Telecom Project Management, Risk 
Identification, Retrieval -Augmented Generation 
(RAG), Mixed-Methods Evaluation, Python. 
I. INTRODUCTION 
A. Topic of Study 
The proposed work involves an empirical study of 
designing, developing, and testing a domain-specific 
Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) system for the 
telecommunication project management domain. Whether 
the project is a national fiber - optic deployment or a cell 
tower installation, modern telecom infrastructure projects 
are deployed in a very dynamic environment that demands 
predictable delivery schedules, multi-vendor relationships, 
compliance with complex regulatory requirements and 
strict financial Service Level Agreements (SLAs). Market 
needs are increasing in velocity and traditional risk 
identification approaches are unable to keep up. This 
investigation is about building an intelligent assistant with 
Python that uses a dedicated Risk Knowledge Base built 
using vector databases and LLM APIs. The software 
product will be designed to complete three basic 
functions:  
(1) parsing of unstructured project documentation to 
create real-time analysis of project risks,  
(2) the synthesis of actionable, contextually relevant 
mitigation strategies, and  
(3) dynamic synthesis of a full, compliance-ready risk 
register.  
The research design of this study is mixed method which 
includes a direct comparison between the quality, 
execution speed, semantic depth, and strategic value 
between AI-generated risk assessments and standard risk 
assessments generated by experienced human project 
management practitioners. 
B. Rationale 
Legacy Risk Management models are vital to project 
management offices (PMOs) in the telecom industry today. 
These models usually involve periodic brainstorming 
sessions, manual input and static risk registers that do not 
automatically update as actual proj ect parameters are 
allowed to "drift" in the real world. This passive paradigm 
has serious vulnerabilities throughout the system. Teams 
often underestimate or discount unusual catastrophic 
modes of failure in the operation or environment. In 
addition, there is a significant lag between detection of field 
risk and developing a mitigation plan that can be 
implemented. This delay in operation often leads to 
incomplete SLA fulfillment, therefore to high liquidated 
damages and increase in the project cost. 
Classical ML approaches have been employed for 
predicting qualitative project overruns where machines 
(SVM) or Random Forests, would predict whether a project 
is expected to run over budget using a fixed numerical 
vector. Generative AI and LLMs provide a complete 
paradigm shift since they have advanced language 
understanding and logic skills. There is an immediate need 
in industry and academia to construct a specific framework 
that combines the reasoning capability of the g enerative 
                                       S25021286_Dimalka_Sewwandi_COM 752_MSc_Dissertation_Proposal 
models with an authenticated corporate knowledge 
database. 
II. REVIEW OF RELEVANT LITERATURE 
A. Background to Subject of Study 
Technical Pillars for Research: The technical pillars for 
this research fall into the intersection of three areas, 
namely, NLP, Information Retrieval, and Enterprise 
Project Risk Management. Transformers use the latest 
architecture that processes tokens using deep multi -head 
self-attention mechanisms, thus making it possible to detect 
complicated interdependencies among very long text 
sequences. With the help of API -based wrappers for the 
Python framework, it is possible to change the parameters 
such as ins tructions, temperature, and top -p to transform 
the base models into deterministic assistants. 
One important drawback of only considering the 
parametric memory of the LLM is that one may not get 
domain-specific accuracy and there may be chances of 
inaccuracies generated by the process. To overcome this 
limitation, RAG helps in chunking the knowledge  from an 
external source and then using the embedding model to 
convert this chunked knowledge into high dimensional 
vectors which are then stored in a vector database. Now 
when the project manager provides an unstructured input 
about some operational delay , the system takes a vector 
form of this input, calculates cosine similarity in the vector 
space and picks out top -k relevant context blocks. This 
context is then added to the prompt context window for 
providing a more accurate answer. 
Risk management processes within the 
telecommunications deployment vector should take into 
consideration special factors, such as permissions from 
civil engineering; access permissions at municipal level; 
complex multi-vendor interdependencies among various 
vendors involved in hardware, splicing equipment, and 
towers construction; and contract SLA performance 
tracking, where delay is costly. 
B. Examples and Critique of Current Research in 
the Field 
Early work conducted on risk classification based on 
machine learning algorithms such as SVM and Random 
Forest was done by standard framework creators; it entailed 
predicting the result being over budget or not based on 
numbers. While the results of such r esearch were accurate 
and reliable enough, the complete inability of these 
algorithms to consume texts and offer recommendations 
remained a serious problem. 
New research in the area looks at the implementation of 
generative systems in a wider corporate context. However, 
such implementation usually uses generic prompts lacking 
any local relevance, causing notable hallucinations when 
used with detailed engineering requirements. For example, 
an ungrounded language model may suggest a generic 
approach to handling a fiber -optic delay, thus totally 
ignoring local environmental restrictions or service level 
agreement terms. Moreover, very few academic papers 
consider conducting comprehensive performance 
comparisons with human operators. Therefore, ther e is a 
need to conduct a thorough hybrid experiment by 
implementing a well-tested software tool and carrying out 
a formal mixed-method assessment of its performance vis-
a-vis human decision -making. New research in the area

III. PILOT RESEARCH STUDY 
A. Hypothesis 
A more detailed approach to the central hypothesis 
guiding the research path: 
H1: The dedicated Generative AI framework, relying on 
Python and based on Retrieval -Augmented Generation 
(RAG), is capable of generating risk registers and 
mitigation strategies for telecom projects that cannot be 
differentiated or even outperform the huma n-expert 
baselines in terms of technical precision, compliance with 
SLAs and projects’ specifics, and operational viability 
while increasing generation speed by a factor of 50+. 
In its turn, the study will be guided by the null 
hypothesis: 
    H0: The risk registers and mitigation strategies 
generated by the Generative AI framework perform 
significantly worse in technical precision and operational 
viability compared to baseline entries developed by 
human experts. 
B. Research Method 
The hypothesis can then be tested through the 
development of an appropriate testing environment, which 
involves setting up a database of 30 separate historical 
instances involving telecommunications rollout. The 
database will comprise unstructured text dat a including 
scope, regional environmental factors, multivendor 
agreements, and target SLA levels . The Execution 
Workflow process is divided into two concurrent 
processes: (a) Human Baseline Generation Path, which 
involves manual scenario evaluation by two senior project 
managers who have received certification, and (b) 
                                       S25021286_Dimalka_Sewwandi_COM 752_MSc_Dissertation_Proposal 
Generative AI Product Path, which involves processing of 
the scenarios through our pipeline.

C. Initial Results 
Technical feasibility is demonstrated in the initial 
evaluation of the RAG pipeline. In preliminary testing 
using a constrained context of 5 test cases, the AI Assistant 
based on Python delivered complete multi -line risk 
registers in less than 15 seconds for each case. By contrast, 
the human benchmark of risk register creation took 
between 45 and 60 minutes for each test case. A 
preliminary semantic lexicon analysis revealed significant 
semantic similarities with established industry standards. 
IV. OUTLINE OF PROPOSAL 
A. Aims of the Investigation 
In essence, the main objective of this study will be to 
develop and test through scientific means a professional 
grade generative AI product designed for automating the 
risk engineering processes within the context of 
telecommunication projects. This study will focus on the 
capability of the software agent to perform sophisticated 
analysis in the project context. 
B. Research Objectives 
The study will address the following research questions 
and objectives to achieve its goals: 
1. In what way can a decoupled Python microservices 
architecture be optimized for use in connecting LLM APIs 
with an unstructured domain vector knowledge repository? 
2. What is the similarity level of AI -authored risk profile 
descriptions compared with those that have been written by 
an expert, using sophisticated embedding and text -based 
comparison metrics?  
3. What kind of results will the risk register produced be 
able to score in a double -blind expert review regarding 
accuracy and actionable nature?  
4. What is the exact processing delay difference between 
the auto -generative workflow and manually assembled 
documentation assets? 
C. Methodologies 
This project will utilize an interdisciplinary and hybrid 
approach to research where a Software Engineering model 
for development is combined with a Mixed-Methods 
evaluation approach. This application artifact will be 
developed with the use of Python. The structural 
components used in this system would include structural 
libraries such as Lang Chain and Llama Index to ensure 
smooth operation of the LLM API. The local Risk 
Knowledge Base will be constructed with the help of an 
open-source vector database such as Chroma DB or 
FAISS. This framework will use a mixed-methods 
evaluation approach to collect both quantitative data 
(Cosine Similarity, ROUGE-L, Processing Latency) and 
qualitative analysis (Blind Expert Panel review on 5 
Likert Scale). 
D. Ethical Considerations 
Given the nature of the study, where all the data is 
synthetically generated and historic anonymization is 
applied to corporations, there will be no risks associated 
with human subjects or breaches of confidentiality. There 
is no transfer of any personally identifiable information 
(PII) using the external LLM API endpoints. All the 
source data, including training documents and risk logs, 
have no NDA issues or corporate proprietary concerns. 
E. Limitations and Scope 
In this case, this investigation is consciously confined to 
addressing only the implementation aspect of telecom 
infrastructure initiatives. It is not an effort to solve large-
scale financial risks, changes in markets at portfolio 
levels, and organizational issues of corporate governance. 
This tool will only be able to interact with cloud-based 
API endpoints of pre-trained LLMs. Developing a base 
transformer network and performing extensive fine-tuning 
of weights is not within the scope of this study. 
F. Plan and Timetable 
The study will start at the start of the academic year and 
will end after a 6 -month duration. Each stage of the 
project’s lifecycle has been systematically planned in 
distinct phases, which consist of literature review, 
configuring the backend pipelines, performing empirical 
testing, and analyzing the data. The following timeline 
gives an insight into the exact critical path and delivery 
phase.

G. Personal Development Requirements 
For the project’s success in its implementation, the 
researcher is expected to undertake the acquisition of 
specific skills in certain highly technical areas, namely, 
Advanced Python Engineering (asynchronous API 
manipulation and validation via Pydantic), Vector Math 
(embedding spaces), and Statistics (non-parametric tests). 
G. Resource Requirements 
The computing resources and logistical support needed for 
this research will involve: (1) Hardware: Local dedicated 
work station with multi-core processor and at least 32GB 
RAM; (2) Software: Python v3.10+, Vector database 
(Chroma DB/FAISS), and commercial LLM API keys; (3) 
Enterprise data: Anonymous historical telecom contracts, 
tenders, and PMBOK.
